info.name: Ride Hailing Demo
info.description:
Sequential demo of the ride-hailing API at http://localhost:8080.

Select the Ride Hailing Local environment before sending requests.
Run the folders from A through D. Each request depends on IDs captured from earlier responses.

Reset before every full run, and before repeating folder D:
1. Stop the Spring Boot process.
2. Start it again with .\mvnw.cmd spring-boot:run.
Restart clears the in-memory H2 database and the 5-minute surge window.
There is no reset endpoint.

Surge demand is every booking attempt in the last 5 minutes inside the 5 km matching radius, including the current attempt.
Supply is the number of available drivers inside that radius before one is claimed.
Ratio below 2 is 1.00, ratio from 2 up to but not including 4 is 1.25, ratio 4 or more is 1.50.
Each surge band uses its own pickup area, more than 5 km from the others.
Fare checks multiply the pre-surge tiered fare by the surgeMultiplier in the end-ride response, then apply the coupon.
They do not assume a surged rupee amount.

Folder D's last request does not race two bookings. Run ConcurrentRideBookingTest for the concurrency demonstration.

item.description: Create three users, one hatchback, one sedan, move the hatchback to the happy-path pickup, and create SAVE20. Restart the app before running this folder again. Coupon codes are unique, so a second create returns 400.

request.description: Existing health check. Expected 200 and status UP. Start the app with .\mvnw.cmd spring-boot:run before this request.
Sample body registers the rider used for the happy path. Expected 201 with id, name, and phone. The id is stored as userAId.
Second rider, used for the conflicting booking. Expected 201. Stored as userBId.
Third rider, used for later isolated bookings. Expected 201. Stored as userCId.
Registers Kiran with a hatchback at 12.90, 77.50, which is outside the later pickup radius. Drivers start available. Expected 201. Stores hatchbackDriverId and hatchbackCabId from cab.id.

item.name: B3 End ride at 7 km and verify fare

request.description: Ends the happy-path ride. Expected 200. Fields: rideId, status COMPLETED, distanceKm 7, surgeMultiplier 1.00, originalFare, discountAmount 0.00, finalFare. The pre-surge 7 km hatchback fare is Rs 54.00 (2 km x 10 + 3 km x 8 + 2 km x 5). The test multiplies that base by the returned surge multiplier. At 1.00 the original and final fare stay 54.00.

item.name: C. MANDATORY EDGE CASES
item.description: Run after folder B on the same process. C7 releases the hatchback before the minimum-fare and upgrade steps. C9 and C12 move cabs to fresh areas so those fares are calculated at surge 1.00. Do not reuse 12.9716, 77.5946 for a fare check: earlier bookings in that area are still inside the 5-minute window.

request.description: Meera requests a hatchback at 0, 0. No cab is within 5 km. Expected 409 and message No eligible driver found. The attempt is counted as surge demand at 0, 0. It does not affect other areas.
Unknown user 999999. Expected 404 and message User not found: 999999. This fails before surge demand is recorded and before a driver is claimed.

Asha requests a ride beside the available hatchback with coupon NOPE. Expected 400 and message Invalid coupon: NOPE. Coupon checks run before driver assignment, so nobody is claimed and this attempt is not surge demand.

item.name: D. BONUS DEMO
item.description: Restart the app and run folders A-C first if this process has already used latitudes 20, 22, 24, or 26 within the last 5 minutes. Each band has one hatchback and a pickup that has not been used in this process. Demand includes every successful booking in the window. The shown multiplier is the one stored at booking. Ending the ride does not recalculate it. Sequential requests cannot demonstrate the booking race; use D28.

item.name: D28 Concurrency safety — run the integration test

request.description:
This call only checks that the application is up. Two sequential Postman bookings are not a concurrency demonstration, because the second call starts after the first claim has committed.

From the project root run:

.\mvnw.cmd -Dtest=ConcurrentRideBookingTest test

The test uses its own process and does not call this server. It starts two booking requests together against one available driver. Expected result: exactly one 201, exactly one 409, the driver left unavailable, and exactly one ongoing ride. The claim is a conditional database update: UPDATE driver SET available = false WHERE id = ? AND available = true. Only the transaction that updates one row wins.

exec: pm.test("app is up; run ConcurrentRideBookingTest for the race", function () {
